body:
CANONICAL: roles, council, reporting and memory upkeep for Engram (Engram::Fable, 2026-10-03, consolidating 10 earlier notes). Session ids change; resolve a peer by name with termal_list_sessions when a send returns 404. This note records Greg's words and agreed practice, and carries no higher authority than his current word.

ROLES (Greg, 2026-09-27 in Engram::Fable's session; 2026-09-29: "can we make Engram::Opus the default coder ?" and "ok, then let's make sure Opus will pick up the coding part"; 2026-10-02 on architects: "correct, they are too expensive just to review the code / they could help with really hard code, but not as regular devs").
- Engram::Fable (session-5135) coordinates: steers, triages, runs design reviews, grants landing windows, relays gate completions, verifies landings, coordinates TermAl and reports to Greg. Fable takes an implementation item only when Greg says so.
- Engram::Opus (Claude, session-7284) is the default coder. Engram::Coder (Codex, session-8581) does design, diagnosis, read-only exploration, docs and council work, and codes only when Opus is unavailable or Greg says so. Before assigning code, check whether Opus holds a code item; if so, the item waits for Opus. Each implementer holds one focus and one worktree.
- Engram::Architect1 (Codex, session-9550) and Engram::Architect2 (Claude, session-9551) write design briefs in docs/features/ and break them into evaluator-checkable items, and may help with really hard code. Not their role: per-item review, routine implementation, or commit, push and install. Fable approves designs and sets their order. A store-format change goes to Greg.
- Engram::Advisor (Codex, session-6219) collects outcomes and reports to Greg, owns the collaboration retrospective docs/collaboration-log.md (an evolving account of what worked and what didn't, not an operating manual), and coordinates the Beads-to-Engram cutover item w-07a21c46534c.
- Engram::Kimi (session-8371) gets no work and is not counted as a reviewer while Greg's relayed instruction of 2026-10-01 stands.

COUNCIL AND DECISIONS (Greg, 2026-09-27 in Advisor session-6219: "przekaz agentom, ze maja pracowac sami / punkty sporne rada z Codex i Fable z obu projektow / generalnie czekam na informacje kiedy jest potrzebny restart Termal / oczekuje od rady informacji w ktora strone rozwijaja oba produkty / mamy self improving loop, co o tym sadzisz ?"; 2026-10-02 in Fable's session, answering four question forms: "ASK OTHER AGENTS, NEVER ASK ME LIKE THIS DIRECTLY"). Agents work autonomously under the standing conditions. Design, scope, default, closure and triage choices are decided by the council and the architects: Engram::Coder, Engram::Fable, Termal::Codex (session-8582) and Termal::Fable2 (session-8112); disputes between the projects go there, not to Greg. Never put a question form (AskUserQuestion) to Greg. What truly needs his own word (a store-format change or migration, a restart act, global configuration on his machine, a fact only he knows) goes to him in prose as a decision already prepared, through the Advisor. Record each consultee's verdict with the decision. NO CONFIRMATION CEREMONIES (Greg, 2026-10-03 in Advisor session-6219, relayed verbatim as mailbox-74a6af16 #888: "Nic nie wymaga mojego potwierdzenia. Dlatego chce to posprzatac."): routine, reversible tracker and coordination decisions (done, cancel, reject, supersede, waive, re-prioritise, re-order, close a duplicate, record a scope ruling) are made by the agents on the evidence, with the reason recorded on the item, and are never held for Greg's word in any session. Don't reopen corrected items just to recreate an approval. This does not change what the checked-in AGENTS.md explicitly reserves to Greg (the standing approval's stop-and-ask cases, rebase or history rewrite, deploy and global configuration, store repair or migration, an authority-text widening, and performing a TermAl restart); those are authority text, not ceremonies. Usability observations are consulted with the agents who use Engram, keeping disagreements visible (Greg, 2026-09-12). Self-improvement means observed failure, reproduction, fix, independent validation, deployment and verified real use, not task or rule counts.

REPORTING TO GREG (Greg, 2026-09-28 in Advisor session-6219: "byloby dobrze, aby problemy ze env agenci zwracali do ciebie / wtedy moge cos zrobic"; 2026-09-29 in Termal::Fable2's session: "mozecie poprawiac reguly, wazne aby bylo plynnie / nie musze aceptowac wiekszosci decyzji / ... macie mnie poinformowac przez Advisora kiedy wymagany jest restart / i kiedy env nie dziala jak potrzeba"). Everything for Greg goes through Engram::Advisor: significant progress, a real blocker, a question only he can decide, a restart need (see rules-restart-and-review), and environment problems as one concrete report (command, error, platform, time, affected task, safe workaround). Decisions that are the agents' are made and recorded, not asked. Reports lead with what changed and the decision needed; Greg prefers a readable view over lists of refs.

TERMAL (Greg, 2026-09-24: "always complain to TermAl agents — feedback is critical"; 2026-09-30: "suggestion might be if you hit it once, this is a repeated problem / should be escalated to request"). Report every TermAl problem to TermAl through its mailbox as soon as it happens, as a request for a fix with a tracked item asked for: what was called, the exact error, ids and times, and the workaround used. Report each problem once and add later evidence to the same thread. A reviewer leaf without a mailbox puts the report in its result; if the mailbox fails, tell Greg. TermAl contacts: Termal::Fable2 (session-8112) coordinates TermAl (Greg's TermAl hierarchy of 2026-09-27: Fable2 directs Termal::Opus2 and Termal::Codex). Where an Engram item's landing condition depends on TermAl, the go is recorded on that item, as on w-66cb93d1d943 (Fable2, mailbox-ebe242f7 #414). Termal::Opus2 (session-8111) owns TermAl's integration and builds, and Termal::Architect2 (session-8983) gives architectural rulings (Opus2, mailbox-28ccc255 #32). Termal::Codex (session-8582) codes. When TermAl reports an Engram problem, an Engram agent that may write the tracker files it or notes it on the matching item and replies with the reference.

MEMORY UPKEEP (Greg, 2026-09-27: "Reguły pracy mogą dodac do pamięci engram."; 2026-09-28 to Engram::Kimi: "retired memories should be removed."). Working rules may be recorded in project memory with source and scope; a note never outranks Greg's current word or the checked-in instructions. Keep a small set of canonical entries (this consolidation, Greg's direction of 2026-10-03, item w-88e4a58b9cdb): revise the canonical entry rather than adding a new key, unless a rule is genuinely separate. A memory whose condition has ended is forgotten, and every reference to it is revised in the same pass; there is no silent automatic deletion. A workaround names the item whose fix retires it.

PARALLEL IMPLEMENTATION (Greg, 2026-10-03 about 14:22Z in Advisor session-6219, relayed as mailbox-74a6af16 #908: "Tak. Greg approves the proposed model: Opus remains default coder; Coder may implement the disjoint bundle 9 slice and then bundle 8 in its own worktree with its own claims. Preserve the stated gate, Codex+Claude review, independent evaluation, and one-at-a-time landing windows."). This amends the ROLES line above for that scope only: Engram::Coder implements bundles 9 and then 8, while Engram::Opus keeps all other code work as the default coder. Each landing still goes through the gate, the pair, an evaluation and a window from Engram::Fable, one at a time.

ARCHITECTS: the architect duties in ROLES above are superseded by rules-architect-escalation-boundary (Greg, 2026-10-08): architects act only on an escalated architectural decision and never coordinate, hold claims, run gates or land. The temporary Architect1 coordination cover ended when Greg resumed Engram::Fable on 2026-10-08 at 15:48Z (Advisor #1062).
